definitions.gloss: instant, spur of the moment, split second
definitions.explanation: A very brief moment requiring an immediate, instinctive response. Almost always used in the pattern 咄嗟に or 咄嗟の.

examples.japanese: {咄嗟|とっさ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧こと⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}なかった→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: It happened so suddenly that I couldn't find the words.

examples.japanese: {咄嗟|とっさ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{嘘|うそ}をついて→嘘をつく：21763_usowotsuku⟧しまったこと⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{後悔|こうかい}→後悔：02738_koukai⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I regret having told a lie on the spur of the moment.

notes:
{咄嗟|とっさ} is almost exclusively used in two patterns: {咄嗟|とっさ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (adverbially) and {咄嗟|とっさ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ (as a modifier). It is rarely used on its own.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {咄嗟|とっさ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ + verb: instinctively, reflexively
- {咄嗟|とっさ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{判断|はんだん}→判断：03571_handan⟧: snap judgment
- {咄嗟|とっさ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{出来事|できごと}→出来事：03446_dekigoto⟧: sudden occurrence
- {咄嗟|とっさ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧こと⟦で→で：00502_de⟧〜: it happened so suddenly that ~

USAGE: Implies that the reaction was instinctive rather than deliberate. The kanji {咄嗟|とっさ} are rarely written; the hiragana form とっさ is common.
